text:
angela: quick triage — CVE-2026-4512 shows a vuln in grpc proxy we ship in private images. impact: possible RCE on edge if unauthenticated traffic hits gRPC gateway.
kevin: ok severity? any exploit seen in wild?
angela: GH advisory marks CRITICAL, but only repro with crafted headers. we haven't seen signs in telemetry. affected tags: rwinf/proxy:1.3.{2,3} and customer-onprem/*-2025 images that include older grpcx.
marta: customers on Dedicated w/ VPC and Private onprem: many still run 1.3.2. we need backport plan — can't force rolling upgrades.
kevin: main constraints: onprem images are signed + hashed per-customer. we can't change signature scheme without revalidating KMS policies and onboarding each customer.
angela: propose: patch grpcx in main runtime repo -> create hotpatch branch `hotfix/grpcx-cve-452` -> cherry-pick to `release/1.3.x` and build per-customer images with existing signing pipeline.
build-ci: build failed for release/1.3.2-hotfix: missing build arg `KMS_KEY_ARN`. CI log: ```ERROR: missing KMS_KEY_ARN env
at docker build ...``` 
kevin: that's expected — onprem images rely on customer KMS integration during signing step. For Dedicated we can push a generic patch image, but Private customers require their key.
marta: ops note — our signing job expects kms role in vault path `secret/onprem/<customer>/kms`. Some customers have rotated keys; we need to validate keys before triggering builds.
angela: decision matrix: (1) high-risk customers with external exposure -> immediate priority and coordinated key validation + signed hotpatch images (2) low-risk internal-only customers -> scheduled next maintenance window (3) unreachable keys -> create documented fallback: provide unsigned artifact + remediation script and on-prem guide.
kevin: RBAC concern: the patch changes admin API surface for cache flush. On older 1.3.x, RBAC policy key `proxy.admin.flush` doesn't exist. Need compatibility shim so legacy RBAC doesn't break.
marta: can we do compatibility shim in code so old roles map to new scope? sounds safer than forcing role changes across customers.
angela: yes. implement shim + unit tests. also add audit log entries for flush events: `audit.put("proxy.flush", user, ctx)` so we have forensics if exploited.
sec-oncall-bot: reminder: file an incident ticket and attach affected-customer list. Priority = P1 if any public-facing endpoints are exposed.
angela: will open INC-2026-042 and tag infra + solutions. I'll start branch and push PR draft. assigning: kevin (build/sign), marta (customer outreach & key validation), angela (shim + audit + PR). ETA: patch PR by EOD, per-customer build start tomorrow.
kevin: I'll add a CI gate to fail early if KMS path not found and produce a per-customer checklist: key ARN, role ARN, last-rotated.
marta: I'll triage customers and post a list here by 15:00 UTC.
angela: thanks. quick note: for Dedicated cloud pools we can enable automatic fallback routing to `model-proxy:latest-secure` if capacity permits — reduces blast radius while we roll patches.
kevin: noted. I'll coordinate a staged rollout in console: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> all.
marta: ack. ping me on the outreach thread when builds start.
angela: closing loop later with postmortem if we see exploit attempts. :eyes:
